entries.rationale: Module metadata, registry, and non-runtime template support module governance.
Worker processes, queue declarations, and scheduling/reaper paths are execution infrastructure.

Global schemas, shared contracts, and ORM models are accepted platform/storage boundaries for the modular monolith; contracts purity and router ORM checks keep them from growing unguarded feature ownership.
entries.removal_condition: Promote DTOs to module contracts only when behavior changes; keep shared contracts and ORM guarded by boundary tests meanwhile.

entries.rationale: Cross-cutting auth, storage, runtime, audit, notification, tenant, and operator support code is not a bounded feature module by itself.
Supporting audit, tests, docs, memory, and frontend ownership evidence are tracked separately from backend production domains.

scope.classification_rule: Every discovered zone is classified as canonical_feature_module, residual_legacy_feature_boundary, unmanaged_feature_surface, shared_platform_infrastructure, compatibility_wrapper, runtime_process_ownership, accepted_architectural_debt, or supporting_tool_test_documentation_frontend_evidence. Residual legacy feature boundaries remain open modularisation debt until migrated, reduced to behavior-free wrappers, or reclassified with proof. Accepted architectural debt entries track documented allowlisted cycles or facade exceptions and stay open until the underlying refactor closes them.

findings.evidence: app.modules.registry imports account_audit, account_core, account_editing, account_ggr, account_imports, account_jobs, account_lifecycle, account_profile_completeness, account_profile_state, account_proxy, account_safety, account_shared, auth, bought_onboarding, human_behavior, neuro_commenting, story, warmup; no unmanaged feature debt is open.
findings.finding: Backend feature ownership is fully classified under canonical modules or accepted support surfaces.
findings.recommendation: Keep structure audit drift checks required for structural changes.
findings.risk: Low. Keep inventory checks active so new feature-owned code cannot appear unclassified.

findings.finding: Frontend modules expose enforced public indexes and only accepted compatibility deep imports remain.
findings.recommendation: Keep frontend boundary policy checks required for module or compatibility wrapper changes.
findings.risk: Low. Allowed app compatibility imports are explicit, bounded, and documented with removal conditions.

findings.evidence: backend/app/contracts exists for low-risk shared DTOs; app.schemas re-exports moved DTOs for compatibility.
findings.finding: Shared contracts and global DTO/ORM storage boundaries are accepted platform surfaces.
findings.recommendation: Promote DTOs to module contracts only when behavior changes; keep shared-contract and ORM checks required.
findings.risk: Low while contracts purity, router ORM, and inventory checks keep shared storage boundaries from attracting unguarded feature ownership.

findings.evidence: Wrappers include compatibility docstrings and are documented in legacy-wrapper-audit.md, legacy-wrapper-deprecation-plan.md, and legacy-wrappers.json.
findings.finding: Legacy API/service/worker wrappers remain import-compatible with a static deprecation plan.
findings.recommendation: Advance stages only in dedicated compatibility-preserving PRs; do not remove wrappers before Stage 5.
findings.risk: Low while architecture tests prevent modules from importing legacy wrappers.

findings.evidence: Runtime role metadata maps each reserved queue to a dedicated worker role; maintenance_worker maps only to maintenance_jobs.
findings.finding: Reserved queue ownership is logically split into dedicated runtime roles.
findings.recommendation: Keep logical roles narrow and split physical worker services only when production resources allow it.
findings.risk: Low. Resource-constrained staging may still group queues in one physical worker by using raw --queues mode without --role.

findings.evidence: Multiple tests parse imports and source files independently with small local helper functions.
findings.finding: Architecture tests contain duplicated static-analysis helper patterns.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate helpers only when a future boundary change makes duplication noisy.
findings.risk: Low. Duplication is accepted for small, explicit guard tests while architecture boundaries are stable.

findings.evidence: CI, Test Quality, Semgrep, Secrets Scan, SBOM, Trivy, Complexity, Gitleaks config, and security docs exist.
findings.finding: Security baseline workflows and documentation are present.
findings.recommendation: Keep security docs in sync with GitHub branch protection and workflow policy changes.
findings.risk: Low. Branch protection remains a repository setting outside source control.

findings.finding: Machine-readable inventory has no open unmanaged backend/app feature surfaces.
findings.recommendation: Keep architecture debt inventory exhaustive and fail checks on untracked backend/app production files.
findings.risk: Low while inventory checks keep production files classified.
